content.title: The Trap of Loneliness in a Crowd
content.subtitle: Why do I feel like a stranger to myself?
content.body:
The Me Behind the Mask

In the light of day, among people, we are all rather admirable. We dress well, speak politely, and maintain the image of a respectable person.

But when the day ends, the noise fades, the door closes, and no familiar eyes are watching, which version of us awakens in solitude? The sin we fear committing in front of people- do we commit it without hesitation when alone before our Lord?

The Fear of People vs. The Presence of Allah

Do we fear people more than we fear our Creator? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ warned us:

“On the Day of Judgment, some people will come with mountains of good deeds like the mountains of Tihamah, but Allah will scatter them like dust because whenever they had the opportunity to sin in private, they would disobey Allah.”

— (Sunan Ibn Majah: 4245)

Before committing a sin, do we remember that although no one may be watching, Allah sees us? No darkness can hide anything from the One whose sight never fails.

Solitude Is the True Test of Faith

The true test of faith is not found in people’s applause or praise. It is found in solitude, when every door to sin is open and there is no fear of anyone’s judgment.

At that moment, choosing to step away from sin out of the love and fear of Allah is Taqwa.

When the world is asleep, shedding tears alone on the prayer mat, or quietly performing deeds away from people’s eyes, may become the truest reflection of who we are before Allah.

The Door of Return Is Still Open

Secret sins can slowly weaken the soul from within. Yet there is still no reason for despair. The Lord who knows our hidden mistakes also loves to accept the repentance we make in solitude.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“On the Day of Judgment, Allah will bring the believing servant close and cover him with His mercy. He will remind him of his hidden sins. When the servant thinks he is ruined, Allah will say, ‘I concealed these sins from people in the world, and today I forgive you.’”

— (Sahih al-Bukhari: 2441, Sahih Muslim: 2768)

Therefore, let us transform the solitude within those four walls from a place of sin into a sacred sanctuary of tearful repentance. Bow your head privately before the Lord who has concealed your mistakes in solitude.

Never forget: The praise of people cannot save us in the Hereafter. On that Day, we will stand before Allah as the person we truly were when no one was watching.
